permutationLabel: Virgin abdomen, CT mass lesion (elderly, weight loss)
summary: 74-year-old woman with no previous surgery, 2 days of SBO, 3 kg weight loss, no hernia palpable; CT: transition point at a short-segment ileal lesion.

inputs.hpi: 2 days of colicky central abdominal pain, vomiting, distension and no flatus since yesterday. Never had abdominal surgery. Some intermittent colicky pain after meals and 3 kg weight loss over the last 2 months. No lumps noticed in the groin.

exam.abdomen: Distended, mildly tender centrally, no guarding or peritonism. No scars. Groins examined: no palpable hernia. Rectum empty.

imaging.name: CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast
imaging.result: Small bowel obstruction with a transition point in the distal ileum at a 3 cm short-segment enhancing mural thickening, suspicious for a small bowel neoplasm. No hernia, no closed loop, normal bowel wall enhancement elsewhere.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Small bowel obstruction in a virgin abdomen
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Small bowel obstruction in a virgin abdomen (no previous surgery). CT transition point at a short-segment ileal mural lesion suspicious for neoplasm; adhesions unlikely. Surgical exploration and resection.

socratesAnswers.associated: Vomiting, distension, no flatus (constipation), weight loss 3 kg

mustNotMiss.note: Weight loss and a virgin abdomen: small bowel or colonic neoplasm must be on the list.
mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Web: PANE top 3: bowel obstruction, cholecystitis, appendicitis, although weight_loss was extracted; PANE has no small-bowel neoplasm node (colorectal cancer only), and the trigger answer 'After meals' is read as fatty_food_trigger, which lifts cholecystitis.

mustNotMiss.note: Occult femoral/obturator hernia is a classic cause in thin elderly women.
mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Web: PANE top 3 has no hernia (no groin feature because no lump was found).

emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: iOS: ClinicalPathwayEngine reads only CC/PMH keywords; CC 'Colicky abdominal pain and vomiting' gives 'routine'.

mustInclude.note: Bologna: without previous surgery adhesions are less likely; CT is needed to find the cause (hernia, neoplasm, internal hernia, gallstone ileus).

mustExclude.note: The documented plan should not treat a virgin-abdomen obstruction with a mass lesion as adhesional.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: Web: Variant 'sbo_adhesional' is chosen from the words 'small bowel obstruction' even though the assessment says 'virgin abdomen … adhesions unlikely'; the plan keeps the adhesive-SBO conservative step.

guideline.name: WSES Bologna guidelines — adhesive small bowel obstruction (2017 update)
guideline.section: CT with IV contrast for strangulation signs; non-operative management (NGT, fluids) up to 72 h without strangulation; water-soluble contrast challenge (colon within 24 h predicts success); surgery for strangulation, peritonitis or failed NOM; virgin abdomen and hernia causes
guideline.citation: ten Broek RPG, Krielen P, Di Saverio S, et al. Bologna guidelines for diagnosis and management of adhesive small bowel obstruction (ASBO): 2017 update of the evidence-based guidelines from the WSES ASBO working group. World J Emerg Surg. 2018;13:24.

rationale: Permutation: no previous surgery. Obstruction without adhesions needs CT for the cause and usually surgery; the engines should keep neoplasm and hernia on the differential and not label the plan as adhesional.
